The tracker shows the next combo skill over the game and notices on its own what you used. The program only looks at the screen and listens to key presses: it sends nothing to the game and changes nothing in it. The hint is not always exact; the reasons are below.
How the tracker knows what you used
"Skill Usage History" is the main and most accurate source. A skill the game wrote there always counts, but the line appears up to 0.75 s late.
Cooldown slots are the second source. If a skill is on a slot and the history skipped it, the tracker counts it when the slot goes on cooldown.

Key presses, only for skills with "Seen in history or on a slot" cleared in the editor. From the character's key bindings the program recognizes the command of the step the tracker is waiting for and counts it at once. If the history then shows another skill, the tracker corrects itself.

The resource bar (MP, WP, Fury and so on). A skill that spends a noticeable amount of resource counts on a press only when the bar drops: a press the game ignored does not move the step, and a skill pressed early, during the previous animation, counts when it really starts.
To hear keys, run the program as administrator: the game runs with administrator rights, and otherwise Windows does not pass its key presses on.
The history must be turned on: "Edit UI" → the eye on "Skill Usage History". Where it is missing (for example, in the Black Shrine), the tracker follows keys only and makes more mistakes.

The game does not write every skill to the history: chain follow-ups and skills that cancel the previous animation are often skipped. If such a skill is not on a cooldown slot either, clear its "Seen in history or on a slot" flag in the editor, and the tracker will recognize it by keys.

Cheap skills (costing less than a couple of pixels of the bar) and skills the game casts on its own while a key is held count on press and hold without a check. If you pressed the keys but the skill did not come out, the tracker may move one step ahead; the next skill from the history puts it back.
The tracker recognizes only the keys from the game's control settings. It may not understand macros, third-party programs or buttons remapped in mouse software.

The tracker, the layout and the marks over cooldown slots hide when the slots are covered by a game window: skills, settings, the map or a hidden UI. If only some slots are covered, the marks disappear only from them.
The Black Spirit's Rage combo turns on when three rage buffs with a 60 s timer appear in the buff list, and turns off a minute later.
Do not cover "Skill Usage History" with other windows and do not move it: the program looks for it in its default place.

If the tracker gets lost, start the combo from its first skill: it will recognize it and continue from there. If that does not help, use no combo skills for a few seconds: the tracker will start the combo over.
